sec.title: South Korea Warns of State-Backed Watering Hole Attacks
sec.brief: S. CISA adds a Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog South Korea agencies (The National Intelligence Service, the National Police Agency, the Korea Internet & Security Agency, and the Financial Security Institute) jointly published an advisory warning that a state-backed hacking group is actively targeting South Korean citizens and businesses. The warning names two attack techniques: phishing emails and watering hole attacks, and it doesn’t sugarcoat how little a victim has to do wrong. The phishing side runs on two tricks. In one version, attackers disguise themselves as job applicants and send a resume email with a link instead of an attachment, pointing to a blog or GitHub page the attacker controls.
